Date: 10/09/2026
## CC
Cough x 6 weeks, night sweats, weight loss
## HPI
47 y/o M, unhoused x 4 yrs (stays in congregate shelters and outdoors), presents with productive cough x 6 weeks, intermittent blood-streaked sputum, drenching night sweats and about 15 lb unintentional weight loss. Reports a shelter contact with a "TB scare" earlier this year. No prior TB testing on file.
## PMH
- Tobacco use
- No known HIV testing on file
## Meds PTA
None
## Allergies
NKDA
## Social
Tobacco 1/2 ppd. EtOH socially, last drink 2 weeks ago. Denies drug use.
## Exam
T 100.6F HR 98 BP 126/80 RR 18 SpO2 96% RA. Coarse breath sounds RUL. Thin. AOx4.
## Assessment/Plan
1. RUL cavitary lesion with chronic cough, night sweats, weight loss - suspected pulmonary tuberculosis. Airborne isolation in negative pressure room. Sputum AFB smear and culture x3, TB PCR. HIV, QuantiFERON. Infectious Disease consult.
2. Tobacco use - nicotine patch
3. Dispo - SW/CM consult (unhoused). No discharge until ID clears isolation.

pages.title: Infectious disease consult note
pages.text:
## INFECTIOUS DISEASE CONSULT - FOLLOW-UP
Date: 10/13/2026 15:10
Imaging reviewed: RUL thick-walled cavitary lesion with surrounding nodular opacities, highly concerning for active pulmonary TB.
Sputum AFB smear #1 negative 10/11. Smears #2, #3 and TB PCR pending. Cultures take up to 6-8 weeks.
Recommendations:
- Continue airborne isolation. NOT cleared for discharge to congregate or shared living setting.
- Isolation may be reconsidered only after 3 negative AFB smears and negative TB PCR, or after adequate treatment with clinical response, per ID and County Public Health.
- Continue RIPE + pyridoxine; directly observed therapy (DOT) referral to County TB clinic.
Signed: N. Vasquez-Hale, MD (Infectious Disease)
